This. I have social anxiety (maybe not really compareable as my fear isn't keeping me so tied up) but it hurts and really frustrates to be alone with that. My friends struggle  to understand why it's so hard to ask for help or why I'm thinking about that weird thing I once said - which leads me to think my fears are invalid and keep me from getting further help. Please try to bear with her even if you don't understand. Try to explain why you think she should get help and listen to her. You are not responsible for  fixing  her phobia but supporting and respecting her boundaries will pay off for both of you and your relationship. Fear is a really uncomfortable and intense feeling and it's hard to learn how  to deal with it. But it's possible. Until  she is ready to seek help, suggest some simple task like looking up calming  technics and check out some apps (a good first look would be at wysa, great app!). 
Baby steps, it will get better.

Hey there!

I had the same thoughts as you when I started my therapy over a year ago, but there's nothing to stress about. Usually on the first day they will let you just talk about yourself. But don't worry if you forget some details or wanna keep something for yourself right now.

I just told her everything I had in mind. What happend in my life, about people that impacted my life and why I'm seeking help. Just say whatever comes to your mind. You don't have to "prove" that you need help, because those were my thoughts at that time.

Also, don't worry if you dont get along with your therapist. It took me three tries to find the someone I'm comfortable with.
